name: Model context
first: The object that inserts, deletes, fetches, and saves SwiftData models, which a view reads from the environment.

dependsOn.why: A model context saves and fetches instances of SwiftData models.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The class `Trip` is a model, as `Trip` is on the page of SwiftData model.

dependsOn.why: SwiftUI puts the model context in the environment, where a view reads it.
A fetch is sorted by a property, named with a key path.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The value `\Trip.city` is a key path to `city`, as `\Trip.nights` is to `nights`.

what.is: A model context is the object that changes and reads SwiftData models. Its method `insert` adds a model, `delete` removes one, `fetch` reads the models that a request asks for, and `save` writes the changes to the container's store. A model container says where the models are kept, such as a file on the device.
what.afterExample: The context inserts two trips, saves them, and fetches them sorted by city: Lima and Oslo. Then it deletes Lima, saves again, and one trip is left. The container here keeps its models in memory only, so the example leaves no file behind.
what.problem: An app must add, change, and remove saved data, and read it back in an order. A model context does all of that for SwiftData models, and keeps track of what changed, so that one call saves every change.
what.how: The context keeps the models that were inserted, changed, or deleted since the last save. Calling `save` writes those changes to the container's store. Calling `fetch` reads the models that a fetch descriptor describes, in its order. In an app, SwiftUI puts the container's main context in the environment, and a view reads it from there.

when.text: Use the context from the environment in a view that adds or deletes models, such as an Add button:
Don't fetch with the context to show models in a view. A query fetches them for the view, and updates the view when they change.

parts.name: The container, lines 12 to 17
parts.text: A `ModelContainer` sets up the store for the model types it is given, here `Trip`. The configuration `memory` keeps the store in memory only, so nothing is written to a file. Line 18 makes a context for the container.

parts.name: The fetch descriptor, lines 22 and 23
parts.text: A `FetchDescriptor` describes which models to fetch, and in what order. This one asks for every `Trip`, sorted by `city`, which the key path `\Trip.city` names.

steps.text: Lines 12 to 17 make a container for `Trip` that keeps its store in memory, and line 18 makes a context for it.
Lines 19 and 20 insert two trips into the context, and line 21 saves them to the store.
Lines 22 and 23 describe a fetch of every trip, sorted by city. Line 24 fetches them, and line 25 prints their cities: {{["Lima", "Oslo"]}}.
Line 26 deletes the first trip, Lima, and line 27 saves the change.
Line 28 counts the trips that the same request finds: {{1}}.

end.text: The context inserted, saved, fetched, and deleted the trips, and each save wrote its changes to the store.
